Activation patching supports intervention-specific localization, but results depend strongly on corruption methods and outcome metrics ([Zhang & Nanda, ICLR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042)). Successful interventions alone do not establish faithful mechanisms: subspace patches can activate dormant pathways disconnected from ordinary computation ([Makelov et al., 2024](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/70b8505ac79e3e131756f793cd80eb8d-Abstract-Conference.html)). A 2026 preprint further shows that patching effects include interactions with other mediators; component importance can disappear or inflate depending on their states, motivating joint interventions and explicit interaction measurements ([Vaidyanathan et al., 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27510)).

For NextItNet, the relevant structure is stacked causal dilated convolutions with residual connections, enabling interventions across block depth and temporal position ([original paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf)). Proposed adaptation, rather than an established recommendation-specific protocol: freeze each category model; pair histories sharing the terminal item but differing in earlier context; patch intermediate residual states within the final position’s receptive field. Measure clean-to-corrupted restoration and corrupted-to-clean disruption, plus identity patches, multiple matched donors, and selected joint-site patches. Read from the final nonpadding position. Report raw candidate-score margins and ranking changes; avoid normalized recovery when the clean–corrupted gap is negligible.

Donor-support checks should compare activation norms, distances, and downstream states against natural histories matched on length, padding, and recent context. Natural donor activations do not guarantee that their combination with recipient states remains on-distribution. These checks can flag artifacts, not certify faithfulness. Earlier-position effects under terminal-item matching would support history integration for the tested contrasts; endpoint restoration alone could reflect representation copying. Neither finding establishes user intent or predicts training benefit, which requires a separate controlled validation experiment.
